detailed_findings.finding: Closure under addition is handled correctly in all cases r=0, s=0, r+s<m, r+s=m, and r+s>m, with the i=min(r,s), j=max(r,s) device matching the stated Kunz inequality quantification 1 <= i <= j <= m-1.
The cofinite-complement argument is complete: for each residue r>0, membership is equivalent to q >= k_r, so exactly finitely many q are excluded.
The multiplicity and Apéry-style least representative claims are justified using positivity of k_r and the threshold definition of S(k).

reason: The proof correctly verifies the three required conclusions from the Kunz inequalities: S(k) contains 0 and is closed under addition by a complete residue-class case split; its complement in N0 is finite by explicit characterization of excluded elements in each nonzero residue class; and the multiplicity and least residue representatives follow directly from positivity of the k_r thresholds. No substantive semantic drift is present relative to the lemma sketch.
